title: Rollout Harbor: week plan & telemetry bakeoff
executive_summary: This doc is a compact, operational plan for a low-risk rollout lane were calling "Harbor". Purpose: ship the routing + KV-cache tweak with an observability-first bakeoff that compares baseline vs candidate across latency tails and token-cost. Primary goal is to validate the telemetry signals and guardrails before scaling to the broader canary lanes.
rollout_calendar: 2027-04-19 08:00 - Week start standup: alignment and quick risk call (10m)
2027-04-19 09:30 - Preflight run: smoke test suite (infra, routing, model-compat) - owners: Marco/Ethan
2027-04-19 11:00 - Telemetry bakeoff kickoff: start parallel traffic split 95/5 baseline->candidate (duration 6h)
2027-04-19 17:30 - Bakeoff sync: first-pass signal check (latency p50/p95/p99, errors, cost-per-token)
2027-04-20 09:00 - Extend bakeoff to 24h with targeted user cohorts (search-heavy, chat-heavy)
2027-04-20 18:00 - Mid-bakeoff retro: decide whether to widen cohort or shrink traffic
2027-04-21 10:00 - Canary expansion 10% -> 25% if signals stable for 24h
2027-04-22 09:00 - Quiet window: full monitoring sweep + small load spike simulation
2027-04-22 14:00 - Release notes draft finalized and sent to PM/Docs
2027-04-23 09:00 - Final go/no-go meeting; if go then ramp to 100% over controlled steps through 2027-04-25

Validate model variant compatibility matrix - Priya
Confirm rollback playbook is staged and tested in the staging cluster - SRE
Instrument selected telemetry spans for candidate path (cost, token counts, mem usage) - Ethan

telemetry_bakeoff_plan: Objective: measure delta on latency tails, error types, and token-cost per response for candidate change
Traffic split: start 95% baseline / 5% candidate, hold 6h; then expand cohorts; final expansion contingent on signal stability
Signals to track: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx error rate, rejection/timeout rate, per-request token usage, GPU util, KV-hit ratio
Golden prompts: use 40 prompts across Search/Chat/Heading generation; baseline quality measured with exact-match + human spot-checks
A/B log schema: add field rollout_lane=harbor and bakeoff_id=<date>-<uid> to make slices reproducible
Analysis cadence: automated digest at 6h, 24h and daily syncs; manual spot-checks by Docs/QA after 24h
rollback_triggers: p99 latency increase > 30% sustained for 15m in the bakeoff cohort
Token-cost regression > 10% sustained for 1h without corresponding quality improvement
Any customer-facing error with escalations (CS or sales)
Unrecoverable KV cache mismatch or state divergence detected
post_deploy_checks: Confirm post-ramp telemetry baseline matches preflight expectations (within 10%)
Run the quality prompt set and capture outputs; tag any regression for triage
Verify roll-forward metrics: cost-per-token, aggregated/requested tokens, model FPs/FPs in QA set
Hand off summary email to stakeholders with one-sentence verdict and links to dashboards
Schedule 72h retro if any non-trivial alerts fired during ramp
release_notes_draft:
Release title: Harbor routing + KV-cache tweak (harbor-2027-04)

What changed:
- Routing: introduce a deterministic short-path for small-context requests to reduce tail latency (configurable route weight).
- KV-cache: conservative cache TTL tuning for hot prefixes to improve hit rate while avoiding cache thrash.
- Observability: added bakeoff_id tag to request logs and new telemetry spans for candidate path.

Why this matters:
- Expected user impact: lower p95/p99 for short chat queries and search completions, modest reduction in per-request GPU time for hot prefixes.
- Why we did a bakeoff: to validate real-world token-cost tradeoffs and ensure no regression in rare edge prompts.

Known issues / limitations:
- There is a potential 5-8% delta in token accounting for a small subset of synthetic prompts; QA is tracking (JIRA-5728).
- Not yet tuned for very long-context streaming sessions; those users remain on baseline route until further tuning.

Rollout plan summary:
- Gradual ramp with 95/5 bakeoff, cohort expansion, quiet-window validation, and stepwise ramp to 100% if signals remain green.

Call to action for teams:
- SRE: confirm alerts and rollback automation are enabled during the bakeoff.
- Docs/QA: run the prompt set and file any regressions under JIRA-5728.
- Customer Success: be prepared to respond to any user reports during the quiet window.

Contacts: Riley Martinez (owner), Priya Nair (quality), Marco Liu (infra), Ethan Cole (telemetry)
